rationale: No labelled evaluation has been run yet, so there is no evidence the model's sigmoid output is calibrated (i.e. that a 0.7 output means ~70% of such cases are actually fake). A single 0.5 cut-off would silently treat near-boundary, low-evidence outputs as confident decisions. Until scripts/evaluate.py has run on a labelled validation set and chosen thresholds for a real precision/recall trade-off, these are placeholder, deliberately asymmetric-from-0.5 thresholds that carve out a declared INCONCLUSIVE band ([0.4, 0.6]) instead of forcing every borderline case into REAL or FAKE.
